title_en: The man who disputed with Ibrahim about his Lord
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The Quran asks whether the listener has seen the one to whom God had given the kingdom and who argued with another man about that man's Lord.
The other man said that his Lord is the One who gives life and causes death.
The first man answered that he gives life and causes death.
The other man said that God brings the sun from the east, so the first man should bring it from the west, and the one who disbelieved was confounded.
God does not guide the wrongdoing people.

chapters.summary_md: A man to whom God had given the kingdom argued with another man about that man's Lord [c1]. The other man said that his Lord gives life and causes death, and the first man answered that he did too [c2][c3]. The other man then said that God brings the sun from the east and told him to bring it from the west, and the one who disbelieved was confounded [c4].
chapters.body_md: The Quran asks whether the listener has seen the one to whom God had given the kingdom and who argued with another man about that man's Lord [c1]. The other man said that his Lord is the One who gives life and causes death [c2]. The first man answered that he gives life and causes death [c3]. The other man said that God brings the sun from the east, so the first man should bring it from the west, and the one who disbelieved was confounded [c4]. God does not guide the wrongdoing people [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah links the argument to the kingdom that God had given the first man, and the Arabic can be read as because God had given it or after God had given it [c1]. It does not say what the first man meant by giving life and causing death [c3].
chapters.kids_md: A man who had a kingdom argued with another man about his Lord [c1]. The other man said that his Lord gives life and causes death [c2]. He said that God brings the sun from the east and told the first man to bring it from the west [c4]. The man who did not believe had no answer [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the argument ends by pointing to what only God does [c4]. Another is that the ayah closes by saying that God does not guide wrongdoing people [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the name of the man who had the kingdom, his land or his time; the ayah describes him only as the one who argued.
- Not established: what the first man meant by giving life and causing death.
- Not established: whether the first man was a king in the full sense or ruled a smaller territory; the ayah says only that God had given him the kingdom.
- Not established: what the first man did or said after he was confounded.

uncertainties_en: The ayah names the other man, in a spelling that this draft's name check does not recognise, so the chapter texts refer to him without his name; the anchor fixture should be widened and the name restored.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the man who had the kingdom is called Nimrod (Namrud), and later works add details of his kingdom and his end.
Hadith to add later: reports about the argument and the man's end, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
